results.name: E multi-tab comparison
results.output: The Garden pilot study included 42 volunteers and showed a 12% reduction in water use over six weeks without a randomized control group, indicating a design limitation. In contrast, the Garden replication study conducted a randomized twelve-week trial involving 210 gardens, reporting a 2% reduction in water use, but the 95% confidence interval suggesting a range from a 3% increase to a 7% decrease indicates inconclusive evidence of a beneficial effect. These studies differ in their design and results, with the pilot having a different control setup and the replication having wider and ambiguous outcomes.

passages.text: The pilot included 42 volunteers and reported 12% lower water use over six weeks. It did not use a randomized control group.
A randomized twelve-week trial with 210 gardens estimated a 2% reduction. Its 95% confidence interval ranged from a 3% increase to a 7% reduction. This did not establish a clear benefit.
